summary: Kōichi Furusaka specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Hakuyu Hadano and served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University.
Laeticia Söderman focuses on Buddhist studies and Japanology. She was a graduate student at the University of Helsinki, where she earned her M.A. by 2010.

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Banaras Hindu University, University of Allahabad, and Gorakhpur University under Govind Chandra Pande, he was later a visiting professor at Haverford College (circa 1983–1984).
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indologist. He held positions at the Oriental Institute in Vadodara and worked as a Jain Pandit at the Baroda Central Library.

Lama Palden Drolma specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She received traditional instruction from teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (until circa 1989) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Schmithausen (born 1939) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker, later serving as professor at the University of Münster (circa 1970–1973) and the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University by 1986 and became a professor at the University of San Diego around 1988.

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the University of Manchester (circa 1970–2000), Wolfson College and the University of Oxford (circa 2000–2015), and served as president of the Pali Text Society (circa 1994–2002).

Lang Chen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at Yale University (circa 2008–2015), studying under doctoral supervisors Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, as well as teacher Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Temple University until around 1993, supervised by Charles Wei-hsun Fu and taught by Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Lara Braitstein focuses on Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She completed her PhD at McGill University (circa 1997–2004) under Richard P. Hayes and also studied under the traditional teacher Mipham Chokyi Lodro.

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Minnesota (circa 1977) and held positions at the universities of Minnesota, Washington, Hawaii, and Chicago, as well as Langara College (circa 1989–2012).

Lars Fogelin works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and later held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse (born 1950) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg University, the University of Bonn, and the University of Oslo (circa 1971–1997), where he also held a teaching post.

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Ganden Shartse Monastery until circa 1959, he served as its abbot (circa 1976–1984) and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (1976–1977).
Latika Lahiri (1923–2008) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (1958–1959) and held a post at the University of Delhi beginning in 1959.

Laura Harrington specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Columbia University (circa 1995–2002) under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teachers including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, and Lobsang Jamspal.

Lauran Hartley specializes in Tibetology. She has held posts at Indiana University (circa 2001–2003), Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (circa 2003), Rutgers University, and Columbia University (circa 2007).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied medicine at the University of Glasgow, later holding posts at Medical College Kolkata (1896–1902), the British Army (1904), and University College London (1906–1908).
